items.title: Ask HN: Has AI coding changed who builds your internal tools? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: In a large company, a dedicated team might build an internal tool that dozens of other teams use. If your team needs a feature for its own workflow, you have to explain the use case, agree on how it fits into the shared tool, and wait for it to get prioritised. With AI coding tools, it might now be faster for the team that needs the feature to build and maintain its own tool or completely scratch the tool and rebuild it if need. I'm curious how that plays out once the tool has been in use for a while. So is paradigm shifting where we remove centralisation of building internal tools and let teams decide? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50485228 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Open-source firmware for 2011 Bowers and Wilkins Zeppelin Air (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Just wanted to share something I've built. It's fully reverse engineered, running on an old 2.4 Linux kernel I found on Nokia HD-1, but with a modern all-Rust userspace. Support Airplay 2 and Snapcast. The Airplay 2 implementation synchronizes with real Apple devices down to 1ms in the multi-room configuration. Spotify support is present, but it doesn't work for me because of librespot key issues. It utilizes the MIPS co-processor cores I have found on it for audio decoding and crypto. There's no FPU on the ARM nor the MIPS, so all the codecs are reimplemented in fixed-point math and made to fit the very small shared SRAM buffers. The DSP board firmware is also completely replaced. It fixes all the complaints I had about the original device: no source auto-switching, USB audio would de-enumerate when the speaker went to sleep, volume keys were sending HID events instead of using the proper UAC status interrupt endpoint, etc. I tried getting 24b USB audio to work, but unfortunately the endpoint buffers on this old AVR32 are too small. The the network audio supports full 44.1/48/24b though. The Wi-Fi chip is very old, there's no upgrading that, so realtime ALAC on Airplay or PCM/FLAC on Snapcast can be spotty if the connection isn't perfect, but Ethernet works too. The iPod dock doesn't work, mainly because I can't find my old iPod anywhere to develop against. Send PRs if you have one! Also partly for vanity and partly for UX I updated the LED colors and FX. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50485222 Points: 1 # Comments: 0
